nodes.text: A choice already made
nodes.title: The Temple of Time

nodes.text: Was that... someone crying?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Hey, you’ve already made your choice. Keep moving through the tunnel.
A few years have passed since the Robot Revolution, and things had calmed down, the way a house calms down after a fire: by having less in it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The war had been loud. The peace was not. The cities hummed. The streets were so clean they squeaked. Machines cooked, carried, counted and, more and more, decided, and nobody was cruel about any of it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The street was wet and shining and almost empty. Thin lines of light ran along the pavement like lanes for something smaller than people, and little white carts rolled on errands of their own. A robot stood against the wall of a tower, switched on and waiting for no one. High above, two drones crossed the clouds, unhurried, going exactly where they had always been sent.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The only things that glowed with any enthusiasm were the screens. A fox-eared girl made of pink light watched the street with a patient smile, and beside her a maid in lace did the same. Neither was a person. Both were for sale. Past them, a tower rose above the rest with a star on its face, and the setting sun lay across the whole city in long bars of gold.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: It was autumn, or the city's idea of one: a few trees in their concrete planters had been allowed to drop their leaves.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Nobody shouted anymore, which everyone agreed was progress. The Narrator has noticed that 'everyone agrees' is simply what a room sounds like after the dissenters have left. Anyway. Listen. These people are about to discuss the most important things in their lives.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Just got the new upgrade for my home bot. It can practically cook dinner by itself now.
nodes.speaker: Passerby 1

nodes.text: I heard they're implementing AI-driven governance in the next district. Direct democracy, powered by algorithms.
nodes.speaker: Passerby 2

nodes.text: Have you heard about the new REI model? They’re amazing. Now they even come in fox-girl and maid versions.
nodes.speaker: Passerby 3

nodes.text: That Fairchild Star Lake Institution right, what REI model is this?
nodes.speaker: Passerby 4

nodes.text: A chest stands in a room off the tunnel. Beside it, a door remains sealed.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Strange. I do not remember this being here. You should check it out.
You open the chest. Inside lies a black rod, its dark surface traced with violet markings.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The rod settles into your hand. The ground shudders; stone cracks somewhere beyond the room, and the world falls away.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: A night. A fence. A dirt road that smelled of dust and cut grass, and fireflies. Somewhere in the dark a little girl was crying, the way only the very small can cry: completely, and with no plan to stop.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: sniff… hic… uuu… sniff…
nodes.speaker: Girl

nodes.text: Thank you for saving me.
nodes.speaker: Girl

nodes.text: Hah… hah… You looked like you were in trouble.
nodes.speaker: Boy

nodes.text: And there’s no way I could just leave you be. If anything like this happens again, just call my name.
nodes.speaker: Boy

nodes.text: Thank you.
nodes.speaker: Girl

nodes.text: The memory fades. Back in the room, the chest has vanished.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: A wall has collapsed in the next room, revealing stairs and a way forward.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Looks like there is a path forward open now. Let’s keep moving.
You climb into a hall of white marble and hourglasses, then step out toward the garden. Fire blocks the road. Two barrels stand nearby.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You should hit those barrels. I think they have water in them, this should help with the fire.
The barrels break beneath the rod. Water spills over the flames, opening the path.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Three harpies descend across the path. The figure who has guided you steps into the light.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The path ahead may prove challenging, beyond what you’ve faced so far. Allow me to lend you my strength.
I am Arielle, guardian of the Temple of Time. By my blade, we shall carve a new future, correcting the course of the past.
Quickly… together, we stand stronger against these foes.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Let me lead the way. Your trust grants me strength.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Arielle strikes once, twice, a third time. The harpies recoil, but the fight is not over.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The tide of battle wanes. Summon the full extent of my power… let’s turn the scales.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: You call on the full extent of Arielle’s power. The harpies fall, and another memory takes their place.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: A laboratory, a little after midnight: servers humming, a dozen screens glowing. Coffee was forbidden here. Coffee was also, naturally, everywhere your colleagues were.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Two people were arguing about it, and neither of them really meant the coffee. In a world that had mostly stopped caring, it was the sound of two people who still did.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Again with the coffee in here? You know the rules about liquids around the lab equipment.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Oh, lighten up. It's not like your precious machines can't handle a little coffee. Or is it you that can't handle a bit of change?
nodes.speaker: Female Colleague

nodes.text: Sure, because a fried circuit board is exactly the kind of 'change' we need around here. Very progressive.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Your sarcasm is as stale as yesterday's brew. You really think you're charming, don't you?
nodes.speaker: Female Colleague

nodes.text: Charm? No. But I do have a knack for brightening up this dreary place.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: He winked. She did not find it charming.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Brightening up? Who do you think you are, Casanova? Ugh, you're so annoying. You're lucky Lord Siegmar insisted I be nice to you guys.
nodes.speaker: Female Colleague

nodes.text: Sieg... what now? Who's that?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Forget it. Just keep your winks to yourself and maybe focus on something productive for a change.
nodes.speaker: Female Colleague

nodes.text: I did not ask again. I should have. Ah ...
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: After the tunnel's eerie presence and mystical rocks, the gates were almost too much to look at. Gold, mostly: gates of it, taller than anything the dark had prepared you for, wrought into stars and compass roses and the long feathers of wings, with a low sun burning somewhere behind the bars so that the whole thing seemed lit from within.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Above them the sky could not decide what hour it was. One half of it had settled on sunset, all burning cloud, while the other had already gone to stars, a violet smear of galaxy over towers of white stone. Stone angels kept watch from the pillars. The towers drifted among the clouds as if the ground had been optional. And the floor was polished so smooth that the whole place existed twice.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: There was no one there. Only the gates, the light, and a great golden star set into the floor, as if the whole place had been built around a single point and was waiting for someone to stand on it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Then, between one breath and the next, someone was.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: At the center of it all, small against that much gold, a woman stood with one hand resting on her hip, as if the gates behind her were hers to open. Her hair was the blue of a sky that has never once been rained on. A halo, white wings held half open, golden armor on one shoulder, a cape the color of morning.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Had she been waiting, or had she only just arrived?
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Either way, it was a weight of a different kind, and it settled on your shoulders before she said a word. You had walked a long way to get here, and now someone else stood in front of you.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Well done, Seeker. You have reclaimed your essence, shedding a decade in the process. Such feats are commendable.
Most who walk that tunnel arrive with a great deal less of themselves left.
The gates did not open. They simply stopped being closed.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The way forward is now open to you.
She rested her chin on one hand and studied you the way one studies the first page of a book, deciding whether to keep reading.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Be mindful of the covenant to which you are bound. Our faith in you is considerable.
Your tale, as observed through Arielle’s accounts, promises to be captivating. It would be a disservice to all if it were to falter into tedium.
And Arielle.
For the first time, something in her voice softened.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Mind your training down there. The world below has teeth, and it is fond of things that shine. Come back to me whole, my dear sister.
I will, Master.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: This was how it had gone, the last time he was sure of anything. Beyond the tall glass, the city kept its lights on for nobody: towers, a long bridge, one drone making its rounds across the dark. All of it was clean, and humming, and finished. Inside, the lab kept a different kind of quiet, the blue hush of monitors and the faint sound of a mind being read.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: In the pod, a man lay still. Headphones on, a dark visor over his eyes, so that nothing from this world would get in the way of the next. Seekers were chosen by how their minds sounded, and his sounded like something the Temple could hear.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Across the room, a woman watched the screens, brain after glowing brain, a cup of coffee warm in one hand. She moved the way people move when they have done something many times, or when they have decided not to look at the part that matters.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: It began as a tremor. The floor, the screens, the whole city in the window, all of it jumped at once. It was not an earthquake. Time itself had stumbled, and everything inside it had stumbled too.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Behind the visor, he could not see any of it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The coffee left the cup and hung in the air, a small brown moon, for exactly as long as it took her to understand what she was seeing.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Sparks, then smoke, then silence. Machines survive many things. A cup of coffee at the wrong second is not one of them. That is the version everyone agreed on.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Tsk. And he was one of the promising ones. I have to inform Lord Siegmar right away.
nodes.speaker: Female Colleague

nodes.text: Somewhere between one spark and the next, the room left me, without knowing how or where.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Ten years earlier
nodes.title: Star Lake Inn

nodes.text: The first thing to come back was the warmth. It did not arrive all at once; it seeped in, the way feeling returns to a hand that has been asleep, and it carried a voice with it, soft and patient, calling me up from somewhere very deep. Under my head there was something gentle.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: There was a meadow somewhere close, and wildflowers, and beyond them the quiet sound of water. The air smelled of cut grass and lake. The grass under your fingers was cool and real, and so were the fingers. It was all so far from the cold, humming place you remembered that your first thought was that it must be a mistake.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Hey… hey…
Can you hear me? Please wake up.
Feeling crept back in, tugging me gently out of the abyss. I wanted to answer her. It took me a while to remember how.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You are all safe now, please open your eyes.

You opened your eyes. A woman was looking down at you. She was no longer young; her face was lined with kindness, and with something steadier underneath it. A mantle of brown feathers lay across her shoulders and stirred in the breeze. Silver ran through her brown hair, and at her throat hung a small green star. Her eyes were a calm blue, faded by the passage of time. In the branches overhead, one dark bird sat very still and did not sing.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The sun’s rays, warm but not overbearing, lay across my skin, and a soft breeze whispered through the air.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: My head was resting in her lap, under a tree so wide it seemed to hold the whole meadow in its shade, and its leaves broke the sunlight into a slow, playful dance of light and shadow around us. After the mechanical cold I remembered, it felt almost otherworldly: a pause in the relentless march of time, and a rare feeling of being cared for.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Her smile was warm, and it had a kind of age in it that years alone do not give. It reminded me of my mother.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Umm, who… are you?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Aren’t you a curious little one?
I am called Viviane. And you, young traveler?
I’m … MC-NAME.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: A pleasure, MC-NAME. Welcome back to the realm of the waking. This human world has missed your footsteps.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: This human world? What do you mean?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: She did not answer at once. First she brushed a leaf out of your hair, unhurried, the way one tidies up a child before taking him somewhere important. Then she told you, and she said it as if it were the most ordinary thing in the world.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You, Seeker, have been chosen by the Temple of Time. The path you tread is one I once walked; thus, I am to be your guide.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: I am Viviane Pendragon, keeper of the Star Lake Inn. An envoy of Elizariel brought word of your arrival, from ten years hence, no less. A fascinating twist of fate.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Ten years. The angel at the gates had said it too, a decade, and you had let the word go by the way one lets a strange word go by in a dream. Here, in the sunlight, with the lake breathing somewhere beyond the trees, it was harder to let go of.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The threads of time weave curious patterns indeed. For the coming months, you may call my inn your home, venture into our town, and immerse yourself in the ebb and flow of life here. Among our residents, you'll find company both lively and enlightening.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: For now, you can walk, right? Follow me to the Inn. We will talk more once I have shown you to your room.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: You could, as it turned out. Your legs had some opinions about it, but they came along.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You follow Viviane through the park and into town, toward the Star Lake Inn.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The Star Lake Inn was old in the comfortable way: dark beams, polished wood, and stairs that announced you before you arrived. Your room was at the top of them, small and clean, with a window full of rooftops, and a green hill beyond them, with the lake hiding somewhere behind it. With a little star carved into the headboard of the bed that was already made. Someone had put fresh wildflowers in a cup on the sill.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: As a Seeker, you're bound by a contract … or as Elizariel fondly terms it, a covenant. It's an ancient pact, steeped in responsibilities and privileges alike. Elizariel, with her timeless elegance, oversees these bonds. She's quite the figure, isn't she?
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Alongside this covenant, you've been blessed with a Guardian Angel from the Temple of Time. Though your guardian, seems momentarily adrift, such separations are but temporary. Fate has a way of reuniting those meant to walk the same path.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Excuse me, you have been very nice and kind to me, but I’m afraid I don’t really follow. The Temple of Time? Guardian Angels? Elizariel? Contract? What does any of it mean?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: My memory is quite hazy and fragmented, I don’t really remember what happened. When I think back, I only have some glimpses of the past for the last years. What I do remember, more clearly, is what happened ‘on the other side’ or so it looked like to me, maybe that’s the Temple of Time you are talking about?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: So you told her. The dark tunnel, and the voice that had guided you through it. The girl in pink and white who called herself Arielle. The angel waiting at the golden gates. You found you remembered the angels in some detail. What you could not remember, however hard you tried, was signing anything or agreeing to a covenant.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Ah, I see your journey has already been graced with quite the celestial beauty. Arielle's golden presence and another, draped in the calm of the deep blue sky… Elizariel, no doubt. Your keen eye for their... shall we say, divine attributes, does not go unnoticed. It makes one ponder, had you met me in the springtime of my years, how would your memories have painted me, I wonder?
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: You tried, briefly, to picture it. It was easier than it should have been.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Let not your heart be troubled. Fate has a peculiar way of knitting paths together. Your beautiful guardian angel and the profound covenant you share… these are secrets entwined with the very essence of the Temple, known only to a chosen few. Time has a way of aligning stars; yours and Arielle's paths will cross once more, in the moment most needed.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Then the twinkle went out of her eyes, and for a moment she looked every one of her years, and a good many besides.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Bearing the weight of two timelines, you must tread with utmost care. To cross paths with your past or those from it risks harming both of you.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Heed this warning… your past is a tapestry already woven. Interfere, and the strain may tear not just the fabric of your own being but the reality that surrounds us. When echoes of yourself collide, the dissonance risks unraveling the very essence of time.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Then she smiled again, as if she had decided I’d been frightened enough for one afternoon.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: For the present, let the tranquility of this town be your canvas. As my nephew, MC Pendragon, you hail from the seclusion of the mountains, seeking to weave yourself into the broader tapestry of society here. Embrace this guise, engage with the town and its people. Pick up local jobs and try to meet the local girls, they might spice up your life until this Arielle shall find her way back to you.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: The things a dream remembers
nodes.title: Dreams from the Future

nodes.text: That night the bed at the Star Lake Inn was softer than anything you could remember, and the window was full of stars instead of signs. You meant to lie awake and think about everything she had told you. You did not manage it for long.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You are home again. A small, clean apartment with an overviewing look of the city, a little bigger than one person needed and a great deal quieter, where the walls knew your name and the lights came on before you asked them to.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Everything there was counted. Your steps, your meals, your hours, the minutes you spent standing at the window doing nothing at all. Nobody ever shouted at you about it. A notice simply arrived, polite and final, and the next week there was a little less of everything.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Dinner was made by the home bot. It could practically cook by itself now; that had been the upgrade. It set one plate, because there was one of you, and it never once asked how your day had been.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I had survived a war to sit at that table. Some nights I could not remember why.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The march of progress had outpaced the people it was meant to carry. Cities that were once loud with argument and invention had turned into vast, efficient machines, and the streets below hummed with automated vehicles, a mechanical ballet performed in a silence with no chatter and no laughter in it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: People passed one another with their eyes glued to screens, and the world in front of them faded a little more each day.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: And amidst this mechanized existence, people have lost their drive, their purpose. Ambition and dreams, once the driving force of progress, are dulled by the relentless march of automation. A world where the heartbeats of life. Passion, creativity, spontaneity, is smothered by the chill of technology.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: This existence... it's suffocating. Every action monitored, every deviation from the norm flagged. Step out of line, and you're penalized, constrained by invisible chains. One more violation and …
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Can I truly be alone in my dissent? There must be others yearning to break free.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: “With automation mastered, our next frontier awaits.”
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: And finally, something caught your attention.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Much of the article is illegible. A few words stand out: “Time.” “Mysteries.” “We strive forward.”
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: For the first time in a long while, you smiled.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Since the Automation War reshaped our world, this is the first flicker of defiance, of passion, I've seen.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: And so, the first morning came, with birdsongs instead of a buzz.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Time to pick a job for this week.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: For your first working day, there is a place waiting for you in the inn’s kitchen.
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.action: Work at the Star Lake Inn

nodes.text: The morning passes in a bustle of cooking and serving. By the time your shift ends, the guests are asking who made their meals.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Truly, I hadn't anticipated such culinary finesse from you. Your dishes have become the talk of the inn today, much to the delight of our guests.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Now that you've wrapped up here, the town awaits your exploration. There’s much to see and even more to learn.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: With the day’s work done, you take a walk through Elysium and meet some of the people who call it home.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Hello, I'm running a library in this town of Elysium. I could use an extra pair of hands. You can come work as my assistant. There’s much to learn and discover, even in a library.
nodes.speaker: Arthur Nightingale

nodes.text: Good day! I run the local bakery and could use an apprentice. Roll up your sleeves and let’s get to work. When you're ready you can pick up a job at our place.
nodes.speaker: Henry Crust

nodes.text: Hello there, I manage the grocery store here in Elysium. We need an extra store clerk. Get ready to handle inventory and customers. Feel free to stop by and take your shot at this job.
nodes.speaker: Tom Crust

nodes.text: Hey there! I’m Nathan. We could use an extra hand around the bar. Interested in mixing drinks and meeting people? I might even introduce you to the girls around here.
nodes.speaker: Nathan Fairchild

nodes.text: What do you want? Make it quick, I've got things to do. I don't have time for babysitting.
nodes.speaker: Abigail Stone

nodes.text: Hey there! I'm Christine, the blacksmith. Always got my hands full here. If you're up for some hard work and a bit of fun, come by and we’ll make a blacksmith out of you in no time!
nodes.speaker: Christine Smith

nodes.text: Hi there, I’m a new waitress here. I might spill a drink or two, but I promise I’ll make it right with a smile!
nodes.speaker: Sophie Fairchild

nodes.text: Welcome to our church. If you ever need guidance or have questions about faith, feel free to come by. We're here to help.
nodes.speaker: Michael Carter

nodes.text: It’s really gotten late. Time to head back to the inn and catch some rest.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: At last you return to your room. The town grows quiet outside the window.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: A good day's work deserves a good night's rest.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: It was not much to look at: a tired building at the edge of the city, where the robots in the street were fewer and older, and nobody had bothered to make anything shine.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Ten years earlier, I would have walked past that door with everyone else. I had dreams back then, small ones, and I never did much about them; getting through the day took up all the room. Now, behind that door, there were supposed to be people who still dreamed.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The reception was dim and smelled of old paper. Behind the desk sat a man who had clearly lived a long time and had no intention of being finished yet.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Tell me, child, do dreams still visit you?
Huh, child? The years have claimed over four decades from me, my friend. Childish dreams are long gone, replaced by a resolve to 'strive forward.'
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Yet, there's a glimmer in your gaze, unmistakable and rare in this era. Hope, I daresay, clings to you still.
Boss. We got a new one. He looks to still have it.
We are the Carpenters. State your purpose within our sanctuary.
The voice that answered came from somewhere deeper in the building, and it did not sound like a voice that asked anything twice.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I am looking for something that no longer exists, and maybe, time is the answer.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: You came knocking to our doors for such a reason? I see that you still have it, yes. You managed to avoid the Automation War?
I’m afraid that information is confidential. However, if you do permit me to join your group, I will reveal what I know.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: A negotiation from such grounds? Bold indeed.
Something in the deep voice shifted. It took you a moment to recognize it as amusement.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: At the end of the day, the difference between bravery and stupidity is just the outcome.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: By day, the lab looked almost harmless. Sunlight came through the tall glass and lay across the cables on the floor, across the screens full of other people’s brains, across the pod in the corner, open and empty, with a pair of headphones hanging from its frame.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I can’t believe Boss let you in. Luck's on your side, huh?
Luck's been a strange companion. Never thought it'd lead me here, though.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Lucky, maybe. Yet, not lucky enough to win at chess against the Boss. Our funds must be dire if you're in.
You were part of the Automation War, weren't you? Human survivors are rare. But remember, luck runs out.
She said it quietly, without looking up from her screen.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: As if I chose to survive. I was in Cyber Ops, specialized in AI and robotics. I was supposed to die with everyone else, in the fire the enemy’s robotics division started. Yet, the nihilist got out.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Nobody laughed. Somebody changed the subject, which is what people do when they have just heard something true.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: And still, you shun coffee. The lifeblood of late nights and early mornings.
What can I say? Never felt the pull, especially with its penchant for wreaking havoc on electronics, right?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Some evenings, the ones who stayed late ended up on the old couch in the corner, where the light from the screens did not quite reach. There was a woman beside you, more often than not, close enough that your shoulders touched.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I could never quite remember her face. I remembered laughing, though. I had not done much of that since the war.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Listen up, everyone! We've hit a milestone… the Temple of Time is real!
The Temple of Time?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Precisely, newcomer. A relic granting passage through time, a marvel beyond the reach of automatons.
Wait, really? That sounds great! We actually achieved something, we managed to make a discovery that truly is beyond machines.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Heh, you are still stuck on comparing humans to machines! Imbecile, we are above that! However, there’s a problem. Our colleague who managed to find it… died.
The room went quiet. Beside you, the woman went very still.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You two here are the ones whose brain waves are similar to his. From now on, you will join the experiment as Seekers. You will seek out this Temple of Time, carve the path to that place, and then report back to us.
Another dream, and still no sign of Arielle. I’ll focus on the day ahead and plan during the weekend.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Friday passes in work and wandering. When evening comes, you return to the inn. This time, no dream follows you into sleep.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Behind closed doors
nodes.title: The Black Knights

nodes.text: Huh? No dream this time around? And now it’s the weekend, I can do whatever I want.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Still no sign of Arielle anywhere, I still don’t know what contract or covenant I got myself involved in.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: But this town isn’t all mysteries and covenants. There are some pretty interesting people here... especially the girls. Maybe it’s time for a different kind of exploring.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: You did not get far with that plan. Your phone buzzed first.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Good morning, my dear. Forgive an old woman her struggle with these modern contraptions; a lady such as myself has more interesting tales to tell. Yet it is not stories I bring you today, but a lead. There is something of great interest to you, head to the Military Branch HQ.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Enlisting in the military? Again? It seems history does indeed love to repeat itself. And yet, my memories of the Automation War remain shrouded in fog. What secrets does my past future hold?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: And when you stepped outside, the town had gone quiet. No one at the bakery window, no carts on the road, not even the birds. Elysium had stopped the way a held breath stops, and every street seemed to lean the same way: toward the Military Branch.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Hello, are you a member of the military?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Yes, can't you see these awesome muscles? this amazing helmet? and my big gun?
nodes.speaker: Guard

nodes.text: Ah.. yes, how stupid of me to ask such a thing, but are you guys recruiting? I believe I'm interested in joining the military.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Oh great, another one.... yes, yes, we are still recruiting.
nodes.speaker: Guard

nodes.text: Excellent! What do I need to do to sign up?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: First, we'll need to see if you can handle yourself. Follow me to the training area, and we'll put you through a basic combat drill.
nodes.speaker: Guard

nodes.text: The guard leads you through the building. An argument carries through the door ahead.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The room was all maps and hard chairs, lit by a single lamp hanging low over the table, as if it were listening in. A grey morning pressed against the window, and beyond it the rooftops of Elysium went on with their quiet Saturday.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The older man leaned on the table with both fists, as if the maps might try to leave without permission. A long midnight-blue coat, silver at the shoulders, grey coming in at his temples, and a silver star pinned over his heart. Across from him, a younger man with the same jaw and hair the color of embers leaned in too, one hand open, a gauntlet glowing soft blue on his forearm, trying very hard to be heard.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Neither of them had noticed the door open. It was the kind of argument that had started long before today, and would not be finished today either.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Recruitment numbers are still below projections, Lohen. At this rate, our readiness could be compromised.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Then stop hiding half of what we do from our own people! Nobody signs up to guard doors they’re never allowed to open. If we were honest with them, maybe...
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: Discipline does not need explanations. Our methods have stood the test of time.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Two pairs of blue eyes turned to the door at once.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The younger one had been caught in the middle of a point he would now never finish, his hand still raised.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The older one only straightened a little. He looked at you the way one looks at a point about to be proven.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Excuse me, General, I have brought a new volunteer who wishes to join us.
nodes.speaker: Guard

nodes.text: The younger man’s face changed, and you found yourself wondering what exactly these two were to each other, and, more importantly, what they had been arguing about.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Ah, a potential recruit. You’re just in time to prove me right.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Name?
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: I’m MC-NAME. What’s the argument about?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: That information is confidential. However, if you manage to join us, you might just earn the right to learn more.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Lohen. Since you care so much about our recruits, you can test this one.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Yes sir.
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: Lohen takes you down in the elevator to the training level.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Here, you'll face a couple of challenges to test your abilities. Do your best.
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: Thanks
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: You work through the first of the two training challenges.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Not bad at all, that might even be a new record for the recruits.
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: You finish the second challenge. Before Lohen can answer, an alarm erupts and the lights turn red.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Damn, things were going too well! We have an emergency. Follow me, we need to evacuate immediately!
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: You hurry into a long corridor lined with windows. Halfway along it, Lohen stops.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Is that… Natalie? Why isn’t she evacuating?
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: You know what MC, I have to take a detour, just keep moving forward and you’ll be out of here.
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: Through the glass, far below, the warehouse floor had turned red. Caged lamps burned along the walls, and in their light a girl with a red ponytail sat cross-legged against the far wall, alone, eyes closed, hands resting open on her knees, as if the alarm were ringing for somebody else.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The rest of the floor was moving. Shadows, dozens of them: things that walked like men and things that ran like wolves, something with far too many tails, something crawling along the wall behind the pillars. Every one of them was turned toward her.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She was beautiful, and I could not look away from her, not even for a moment. She did not move and I could tell, this Natalie was in trouble, yet strangely still in control.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: What are those?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: You don’t need to find out. It looks dangerous; just go!
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: Lohen turns away toward the warehouse. You follow the corridor toward the exit. Behind you, a scream cuts through the alarm.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Lohen, noooooooo!!!!
The evacuation lift refuses to open. ACCESS DENIED glows on its panel. The only way left is back.
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.action: Go back for Lohen and Natalie

nodes.text: The corridor is darker now. Down the circular stairwell, shadows gather around the steps.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Are these the shadows I saw?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: The warehouse was chaos. Red lamps stuttered along the walls, shots cracked off the concrete, and the floor between them was alive with shadows.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: At the edge of it all stood Lohen, helmet still on, smiling like a man in a pleasant dream. A woman made of shadow stood close in front of him, fox ears and a long ponytail, her dark fingers resting on his face as if she had every right to them. And behind him, her arms around his shoulders, was someone else: red hair, dark wings, and… a smile.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Across the floor, his sister knelt behind a rifle, teeth bared, firing again and again into the dark, while a creature made of fire leapt from shadow to shadow beside her.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: LET GO OF MY BROTHER!!!!
nodes.speaker: Natalie Blackwood

nodes.text: It did nothing. For every shadow she put down, another rose in its place, and even when the fire burned one away, there were always more.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: And then, between one shot and the next, the woman at Lohen’s back was gone. You had not seen her leave.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I need to help them! But how?!
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: If ----ing you -- a ---, I w--- ----ly --come - sin---
If ----ing you -- a ---, I w--- ----ly --come - sin---
If ----ing you -- a ---, I w--- ----ly --come - sin---
Ah, that Black Rod!!
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: In all that chaos, you remembered it: something that should not exist in this world, and yet it was yours, and yours alone.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: With it in your hand, for the first time you felt you could be of some use against this onslaught of shadows.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Somewhere in the dark, a voice laughed, and it was not coming from any of the shadows you could see.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Looks like we have uninvited guests…
Don’t spoil my fun. I’m still collecting my reward for all this.
After all, there are so many delicious ‘treasures’ down here... Miss Redhead included.
The Black Rod breaks through the advancing shadows. Ten fall before you. Then the gunfire stops, and the remaining shapes flow together into a single figure.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You know, I think I’ve just found the best treasure of all! Hahaha.
She darts through a door at the side of the warehouse and disappears.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The danger had not passed. For a moment there was relief, but only for you.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: With Lohen finally released from the Shadow’s seduction, Natalie had dropped her rifle. She was on her knees, one hand flat on the concrete, the other clutching at her chest.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Thin red lines glowed under her skin, at her throat and across her hand, like cracks in a stove with the fire still going. Whatever the succubus had left behind in her was burning, and she was fighting it with everything she had left, which was not much.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She looked as if she were burning, in pain, suffering. So I decided to approach her.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: But when I got close, what I saw was not so much pain as something else entirely.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She... got... into... my... mind...
nodes.speaker: Natalie Blackwood

nodes.text: She looked up at me as if she could not decide whether I was help, or the next thing she would have to fight.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Or, as I looked at her, for one brief second the word that crossed my mind was ‘devour’.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Ahh… aaa …… ahhh ...so...warm...can’t...think...
nodes.speaker: Natalie Blackwood

nodes.text: Her eyes would not settle on you. Whatever the succubus had lit in her was still burning, and it was winning.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Natalie is still struggling. The succubus has fled into the next room.
Ahh… aaa …… ahhh ...so...warm...can’t...think...
nodes.speaker: Natalie Blackwood

nodes.text: Ahh…aaa ……no... more... please... it's too... much...
nodes.speaker: Natalie Blackwood

nodes.text: Lohen is unconscious. With Natalie still struggling and the demon loose, you follow it into the next room.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The room beyond the door was small and red, and in it, a circle of pale blue light burned in the floor. It looked like a magic circle, and it seemed to be draining the life out of whoever knelt before it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Behind that circle, on her knees and chained to the wall, was the girl in pink and white who had called herself Arielle.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Her wings hung torn and ragged behind her, and white feathers lay scattered across the concrete. The succubus was bent over her, one hand tilting Arielle’s chin up, as if she were deciding where to begin.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: One does not often get to take such a treat. The previous two were surprisingly delightful, but you, my dear, you’ll be the crème of this dessert.
She might not have heard you approaching. Her shadows did.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: They had been waiting on either side of the door, and they were done waiting.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Twelve shadows crowd the doorway. You fight your way through them with the rod, clearing a path to Arielle.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Your blow landed. The succubus came apart into a cloud of dark mist, and the mist slid away into the cracks of the walls, laughing, until nothing was left of her but the smell.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Arielle was still on her knees, her arms chained above her head. The spell circle was still active.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Whatever the succubus had started was still inside her; you could see it in the way she breathed, short and shallow, as if the air itself had become too warm.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The last time I had seen her, she had stood beside me with a promise to carve a new future. Now her wings were in tatters, her arms were scraped raw against the chains, and there were tears on her face that she did not seem to know about.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I had never wanted to hurt anyone as much as I wanted to hurt whoever had done this to her.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Ahh….MC-NAME?...
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Arielle, are you all right?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: I… yes… no … ahh…. Come… closer….
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: It’s okay, I’ll get you out of here.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: In that moment, you wanted nothing more than to get her out. You steadied her with one hand at her waist and reached for the cuffs with the other, trying to work out how they opened. You never did find out.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Arielle leaned forward as far as the chains would let her and kissed you.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: It was not a gentle kiss, and it was not a long one. It tasted of salt from her tears, and of something warm that did not belong to her.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Then her halo brightened, and the first sparks lifted from her hair.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Then she began to shine. It was a gentle light, like morning on the lake, and she smiled against my lips, tired and a little sorry, while she came apart into thousands of tiny sparks.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: For a moment the sparks hung in the air between us. Then the chains were empty.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I was still reaching for her when the last of them went out.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You step out of the chamber. The alarm stops.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The warehouse was full of soldiers now, and every rifle in it was pointed at you. Of Natalie and Lohen there was no sign at all.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: MC-NAME, what are you doing here? Give me two reasons why you should still be breathing. You have 30 seconds.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Then your legs gave out, and the floor came up to meet you somewhere near the General’s boots.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I... need water...
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Get him some water.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: A soldier came running with a canteen. You drank most of it lying down; the rest went down your shirt. Nobody lowered their rifle.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Let's restart that clock. What are you doing here, MC-NAME?
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: There were shadows... everywhere. They attacked Lohen and that girl. There was a beautiful girl with red hair down here, fighting them.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Don’t make me repeat myself. What were you doing in the other room?
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: I wanted to help. The shadows gathered together and moved into that room. I chased after them and... defeated the monster.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: What was in that room?
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: A woman... a crazy woman, but she wasn’t just a woman… she was a monster, with unnatural ears and blinding speed. With every attack, I felt as if a part of my soul was shattering...
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: How were you able to face that? Where is she now?
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: You had no strength left to stand, so you held it up from the floor instead: a short black rod, plain at first glance, with thin lines running along it that caught the cold light of the lamp and glowed a faint violet. Every rifle in the room followed it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: With this. After I hit her, she turned into a dark cloud…
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: What?
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: The first thing to come back, this time, was the smell: disinfectant, starch and, somewhere underneath it, smoke. You were lying in a narrow bed, the first in a row of five, in a long room where the lamps had been turned down low.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: In the bed beside yours, Natalie lay asleep with her red hair spread across the pillow, very pale and very still. Beyond her, Lohen sat propped up against the headboard, bandaged and awake. And at the foot of your bed stood the General, arms folded, looking at you with something that was nearly concern and was trying hard not to be.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You’re finally awake. It seems you passed out.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Where am I?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: In our infirmary, and present here is the beautiful princess you rushed to save.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Comes in, aces all the new recruit tests and then goes for my sister, this guy really wastes no time eh? Haha
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: General, what was that? Even I was unable to deal with those shadows. Natalie was in danger and even now she’s not conscious.
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: If it wasn’t for MC-NAME rushing back to us, who knows, maybe she wouldn’t even be alive anymore. I can’t believe this happened, what’s going on?
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: Under normal circumstances, this would end here, and you would be forced to forget everything that happened. However, I decided to take into account your suggestion from this morning, Lohen. Be proud.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: It was the closest thing to praise Lohen had heard from his father in a long time, and he did not seem to know where to put it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The following is strictly confidential and top-secret information. If you share this with others, you forfeit your lives.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: What you experienced was a demonic attack.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: What??
nodes.speaker: You and Lohen

nodes.text: Silence. Listen. In this world, while we cannot be certain that divinity exists, we have found plenty of evidence regarding demons.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: These creatures love to torment mankind. They enjoy seeing us suffer for reasons we don't fully understand. They often attack our society or try to create discord from the shadows.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: To counter them, a worldwide secret military organization has been established. We collaborate with the church to defend humanity from demonic assaults. Our organization is called The Black Knights.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: While fighting against these atrocities, we also keep an eye open for evidence that might point us to the divine. Lohen, you were often curious about which branch of the military Natalie was part of and why you two couldn’t work together. I'm sure you can put two and two together now.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: My sister is part of a global cooperative military action?
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: If we are so comfortable with each other, WHY DON’T WE HAVE WORLD PEACE THEN? There’s no way this is real!!
nodes.speaker: Lohen Blackwood

nodes.text: It's a crude strategic move, which I’m sure even you, MC-NAME, have heard of: the enemy of my enemy is my friend. Of course, friends only under special circumstances.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Based on the feedback from the base, we were attacked by a succubus. This type of demon uses seduction as its power, influencing people, and some are even capable of entering others’ minds.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: That’s what the pretty girl said. She said that thing entered her mind!!
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Yes, that makes sense. The ‘pretty girl’ has a name; it's Natalie.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: For a moment there was a father in his voice. Then the General came back.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She was assigned to watch over an artifact we uncovered in our last expedition into the demonic zone. I suspect this succubus managed to get it and then escape.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: This is very infuriating, as it happened right in our base. We will need to launch other expeditions to try to recover this artifact that was stolen.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: What did it look like? Maybe I’ve seen it while fighting the succubus?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: If you’d seen it, you would’ve known. It was a strikingly beautiful mix of white and gold, with soft pink running through it. The moment you see this artifact, you’d know for sure it has something divine in it. However, we weren’t able to make it cooperate, or to figure out its true nature.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: On the same note of ‘artifacts’, that rod you gave me in the warehouse, where did you get it from?
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: I don’t know. It just appeared in my hand while I was confronting that demon. I was thinking about how I could fight her, and then my hand hurt, but in it, I had that Black Rod.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Hmm, interesting. Just to let you know, about five minutes after you gave it to us, while transporting it to a storage room, that artifact turned into a dark mist and vanished.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: You looked down at your empty hand. It still ached, a little.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I suggest you go talk to the priest, Michael Carter. He might have an idea about what it actually was. He is also a part of The Black Knights. And Lohen, as of today, you are going to be a provisional member too. Natalie will show you the ropes.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: MC-NAME, you are not even an official member of the army. As such, you are not a member of The Black Knights. However, if you can obtain a recommendation from the priest, you can work from the church side with Lohen and Natalie.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: Here’s a recommendation letter from me for you to bring to Father Carter. You are free to leave, but remember, this is classified information and not to be shared.
nodes.speaker: General Edward Blackwood

nodes.text: You have received the Black Knights Recommendation Letter from General Edward Blackwood.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: By the time you stepped outside, the day was gone. Elysium had gone to bed without you: dark windows, empty streets, and a quiet so deep you could hear the river from three streets away.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I should go to the church.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: What is this feeling? Something feels like it's calling me... in the church’s graveyard, of all places?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: It’s locked, I should come back tomorrow.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: She was sitting on the old gravestones as if they were a garden wall, her back to you, looking out over the river where it ran on toward the lake. Her hair was the pale silver of moonlight on water. If there was anything else about her worth noticing, you did not notice it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: A full moon hung low over the water and laid a silver road across it, all the way to her. Above her, a dark bird circled, low and unhurried, and did not make a sound.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: A meeting ordained by fate? The beginning of a tragedy?
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Or, perhaps both.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Hello, nice weather, right?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Nice weather, at night? What a way to start a conversation... Genius...
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: It was a clumsy start. You took the leap anyway.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She turned only her head, so quickly that the rose in her hair trembled, and stared at you over her shoulder as if you had just walked through a wall.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You... you can see me?
I know it's dark, but your pretty face is quite visible.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Ok, calm down Casanova, we don’t even know each other yet.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: She looked at you the way one looks at a word in a language one almost speaks. And yet, all I noticed were her eyes; how purple and full of life they were.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: …You... Why are you here?
I wanted to pay the church a visit and pray, but something led me this way.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: I’m MC-NAME. What’s your name?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Nemesia.
She said it as if she had not said it out loud in a long time.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: There's something about you... a demonic influence. It's faint but unmistakable.
nodes.speaker: Nemesia

nodes.text: Demonic influence? What do you mean?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Nemesia came closer, her eyes narrowing as she examined you.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Let me show you.
nodes.speaker: Nemesia

nodes.text: She stepped even closer and laid her fingers on the back of your hand. They were cold, and then they were not.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Your hand began to warm, and then to burn from the inside. When the pain let go, the Black Rod was lying across your palm as if it had always been there.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: This rod... it appeared before when I was fighting that demon.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Interesting. This rod can be summoned. Here's how you can access it permanently.
nodes.speaker: Nemesia

nodes.text: Nemesia shows you how to call the Black Rod into your hand at will.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You should go now. This place isn't safe for you.
nodes.speaker: Nemesia

nodes.text: Wait, how can we meet again?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: For the first time that night, she smiled.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: If destiny wishes it, we will meet again here, every Saturday after 9pm.
nodes.speaker: Nemesia

nodes.text: If ----ing you -- a ---, I w--- ----ly --come - sin---
If ----ing you -- a ---, I w--- ----ly --come - sin---
If ----ing you -- a ---, I w--- ----ly --come - sin---
Welcome back, MC-NAME. It looks like my tip from this morning paid off. You have quite the demonic and divine aura about you now, hehe.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: What do  you mean by that?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Oh, pay no attention to an old lady’s whims. You look exhausted. You should take a shower and get some rest.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: She had already turned back to her ledger. Whatever she had meant, she had said exactly as much of it as she intended to.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: After a shower, you fall into bed. In the dark, something begins to shine.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: In the dark, something small and warm began to glow, the way the sparks had glowed between the chains. Slowly, it gathered into a murmur of light, like fireflies that could not quite agree on a shape.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Viviane... tell her what happened… I need your help...
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: What remains of an angel
nodes.title: Fates Entwined

nodes.text: I had a dream of Arielle, I should find Viviane.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Your cup was already poured and steaming by the time you found her.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You told Viviane everything that had happened at the base: the shadows, the succubus, the girl in the chains, the light. About the graveyard, you said nothing.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Looks like you found Arielle. However, she was attacked by a succubus which tried to devour her.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: You know, these creatures usually appear only in dreams, feeding off the vitality of young men and women. They suck... your energy and leave you dry. However, they are much more dangerous to beings connected to the divine or demonic realm. For them, succubi do more than just drain vitality; they can devour their core.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: They are very dangerous creatures, and I highly suggest you never get involved with one, especially now. Since you have a connection to the Temple of Time, you are no longer a normal human.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: There's still a demonic vibe about you ever since we met. To be fair, I do not mind; if anything, it makes the situation more intriguing. This, however, goes to show just how dangerous those creatures are towards you. You got lucky that one focused all of her attention on everything but you yesterday.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Do you think this might have something to do with my demonic vibe?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: For the first time since you had met her, Viviane looked genuinely surprised.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Oh, yes. Where did you learn demonic summoning techniques? No, this is not just summoning; this is more akin to soul manipulation. It’s something those succubus demons are good at; in fact, you could say it’s their technique.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: I was sort of able to do it since I came back here. In fact, this is what I used to defeat the succubus.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: That would explain your tall tale of killing it in a single blow. Like the succubus' normal magic, if the target is not on guard, this weapon is highly effective against demonic or divine entities.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: When she spoke again, there was no smile in it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: However, be careful how you’re wielding it. This sort of artifact… I do not know how you came in contact with it, yet it contains someone’s soul. Perhaps your divine contract is to free whoever was sealed in there, but that also means you should not lose or break it, no matter what.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Now, coming back to Arielle. By kissing you, she transferred what was left of her core to you. This means you can choose to devour her and take all her power. Of course, you also have the ability to revive her. What will you choose?
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: She asked it lightly, the way one offers a choice between two pastries. She was watching you very closely. Apple Pie oooor CheeseCake?
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I?
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I always pick the CheeseCake, we do both adore that one ♡.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: What the?? Why would I devour her? There’s no way I’m having angel for dinner today, I’m not eating her. How do I revive her?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: You sure? Some girls might like that. Of course, you can do that after you revive her.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Her voice changed when she said it, as if she were reading from a page only she could see.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Ye who shall restore one from core soon, must heed the call of the moon. Under its full glance, you shall take one final chance. Take a bath in holy water, lay your feelings bare, sing praise to the Lord of Days, adhere to the Heavens’ ways.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Alright, then, I’ll check the calendar for a full moon.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Now, a full moon comes back in like four weeks, but poor Arielle’s core won’t last that long, so we have a workaround.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Do you know what else is full like the moon? Round round round it goes?
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Moon-shaped chocolate cake?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: No, no. The sun!
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Wait, what??
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: To make it simple, you have to go out during the day and take a shower with holy water. The initial idea of the ritual was to be a bit more private, but now it seems like you have to go naked in the church during the day. Haha.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: What the… are you sure this will work?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: You’ve got only one way to find out.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: She winked at you, Morri always trying to play all her cards.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: What if someone sees me??!!
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: I think you’ll have a harder time explaining why an angel appears before you than just you being nude. But maybe you can figure out how to have this ritual done in a bit of privacy.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: I’ll head over to the church then.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: The church was older than anything else in Elysium, and it smelled like it: wax, stone and, very faintly, wine. The priest at the altar did not look much like a priest. There was a scar across one cheek and a streak of grey in his black hair, and he held his silver rosary the way some men hold a knife.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Hello, a new face I see. You were not here during the service this morning, but the church’s doors are wide open to all those in need. How can I help you?
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Excuse me, Father, for I have a more delicate matter to discuss, and I wasn’t able to attend the ceremony this Sunday morning.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: What is it about, son?
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: I have this letter for you, and maybe afterward, we could talk in private?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: You handed Father Carter the Black Knights Recommendation Letter.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Oh my, I see. Please follow me.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Mister MC-NAME, it appears you’ve gotten yourself involved in a very complicated situation.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Yes, it seems quite complicated. I can’t say I fully grasp all that’s happening yet.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: That’s understandable. After all, you are a civilian, and one without any connection to the divine at that. It’s quite shocking that you managed to survive an attack, let alone confront a demon by yourself.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Yet despite your somehow miraculous survival, Mister Edward Blackwood would like for you to participate in further exploration of the demonic zone.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: And without exposing his precious military to any political stress, he expects me to grant you permission and accreditation from the church’s side.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Is this possible?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Of course not. We are responsible here. We aren’t just going to send people to hell because we can. We value our members and are fully aware of the dangers in the demonic zone. Once you die over there, your soul might get trapped by one of the demons and dragged to hell.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: And that’s not a fate I wish to bestow on any civilian. Only those with a strong conviction in God or a connection with the divine can receive the blessing and accreditation of the church.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: And I have none of those?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Correct, you are lacking, my son. You’ve got none of those except a large amount of luck. And luck alone is not going to bring you salvation.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: General Blackwood mentioned that the demon that attacked the facility stole an artifact that was possibly connected to the divine. If I were in its presence, wouldn’t I be able to have some ‘connection with the divine’? After all, I was close to it.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: What are you talking about? There’s no such thing in the letter! Do not blaspheme in my church.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: I see. If you don’t believe me, how about we try something?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: What? Now you’re going to talk to God and tell me what He says?
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Haha, not quite, but for this I need your help, Father.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: So you want to prove yourself, yet want help before even beginning?
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Yes, well, I had a vision last night.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Right, a vision from a demon!
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: In it, I saw that I can prove myself to you for the Black Knights, but I require Holy Water, about 5 liters, a chamber to myself where the sun shines, and a song that praises the Lord. Does this sound like blasphemy, Father?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: I’ve heard worse.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Is it possible to arrange this? I believe in thirty minutes I’ll be able to prove everything to you, and if I can’t, then I’ll take it as my failure to convince you and won’t bring this topic up again.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Do you even know any songs that praise the Lord?
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: No
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Father Carter drew a long breath, the kind that usually ends with someone being shown the door.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Nobody had heard her come in. One moment there were two of you, and the next there were three: a young woman standing by the door, watching you. She might have been there all along.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She wore a deep indigo hood stitched with small gold moons, and beneath it her hair fell long and black. Paper charms and little bronze trinkets hung from her sash and chimed softly whenever she moved. Beside her, a few cards drifted in the air on their own, glowing a faint, cold blue, as if they were waiting to be asked something.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She smiled at Father Carter as though she already knew how this conversation would end, and at you as though she already knew how you would start it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Hello, Father. Pardon my intrusion in your private chambers. And hello to you as well, fellow member of the church.
I’m not in a good mood now, Ayumi.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: I know. I haven’t seen you this riled up in a long time. However, I did perform a divination last night, and that’s why I’m here today.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: Great, another one that spews blasphemy in my church.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: I’m Ayumi Takashi, also a member of the Black Knights. I mostly act as a scout of sorts, and my ability allows me to gaze into the threads of destiny. And what’s your name?
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: I’m MC-NAME. That’s quite an interesting ability.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Thank you. Now, for my divination. I received a sign last night that someone will come to this church today who will bring us good fortune.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: That’s it?
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Yes, and since this morning, I’ve been camping near the entrance, scanning people. I know that you, Father, have had a hard time these past two weeks, so you become stressed very fast, especially if that person is a newcomer.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: And I believe this handsome man might just be whom my divination foretold!
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: You sure you aren’t just looking for eye candy, Ayumi? You’re at that age.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Maybe? Wait, no, I mean, no!
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: And I’ve even got a book of songs. For some reason, I checked some holy songs last night, just felt like it.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: Ayumi gave you a book: Religious Songs.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Fine, you’ve got thirty minutes to make it work, hotshot.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Wait, about the room and Holy Water?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: We have an older chapel on a higher floor. You’ll find some Holy Water there. Nobody else goes there since it’s mostly used as a warehouse for the church; only Ayumi and I go there. We should really clean that place up sometime. It has a balcony, so you can get your sunshine from there.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Thank you!
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: In the old chapel, you push a barrel of holy water toward the sunbeam falling from the balcony. Ayumi’s book lies within reach.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The holy water was cold enough to make you gasp. You hummed the one song in Ayumi’s book you could half follow, standing naked in a sunbeam in a forgotten chapel, and felt entirely ridiculous. Then, quite suddenly, you did not.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The light around you turned gold. It gathered on your skin, then lifted off it the way sparks lift from a fire, and drifted up toward the balcony. Up there, piece by piece, it remembered how to be a girl.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She was sitting on the balcony rail in a pink dress, pale and swaying, as if staying upright were something she had to keep deciding to do. Water ran from her hem in thin threads and pattered onto the floor below.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: It’s been a while, MC-NAME. Thank you.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Yes, you’re welcome.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: While I’d like to apologize for appearing in this attire and state in front of you, it seems you’re even more shameless than me.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Yes, about that, this is what Viviane told me to do to return you back to normal.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Did she tell you what you should do to me afterward?
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: No, actually no, I was more interested in making sure you were safe first.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Thank you
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Then her hands slipped from the rail, and she fell. I do not remember crossing the room. I remember that she was lighter than I expected, and that I caught her.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She lay in my arms on the flooded floor, soaked through and shivering, her wings spread out across the puddles. She was warm, much warmer than she should have been, and she did not let go.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Up close, she looked less like an angel and more like a girl who had been through something terrible and was only now realizing it was over.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: I’m supposed to be your Guardian Angel, and here you are, protecting me. I’m a sorry excuse for an Angel.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: It’s all right, we all have bad days.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: I’m in a weakened state right now. That creature drained most of me, and it will take some time to recover.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Master Elizariel taught us that when we are in deep trouble, we need the Essence of Virtue to get better.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: I feel like, I’m corrupted, almost defiled, and I can barely fight my earthly desires. I’ve never been so close to falling before, I’m scared.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: I have my own life to live, but I’m sure the two of us are tied together. Where can I find these Essences of Virtue?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: They should be scattered in what humans these days call the ‘demonic zone,’ a dangerous place where not many people have access.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Oh, about that, I can get access to it, but I need to prove to this church’s priest that I have a connection to the divine to let me in.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: I suppose this might help.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: She took the hem of her dress in both hands and tore a strip from it. It came away without a sound, as if the world was not meant to hear it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: While my core was a part of you, it was hidden so that people wouldn’t notice your divine connection. But with this, a church priest should be able to realize that it’s not normal cloth. You can present this as your evidence.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: Is it ok to rip that up?
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: She looked up at you, and for a moment it was not quite the angel looking. Her breath had gone short, her cheeks were flushed, and her fingers had tightened in the torn cloth as if it were the only thing keeping her on the right side of something.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: ahh… I want to rip much more of it up… help me… do that…
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: You never got to answer. A light started at the tips of her wings and ran inward, along the feathers, through her hair, down the wet folds of her dress, the same gentle gold you had seen between the chains.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She looked almost relieved, like someone who had been fighting very hard, and had just been told she was allowed to stop.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: She held on to your hand as long as she could: until the very last spark, a little tighter than an angel should.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Then your arms were empty, except for a scrap of pink cloth, still warm.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: The chapel was very quiet after that.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Viviane, at least, had seemed to know exactly how this would go.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: You dress and carry the strip of pink cloth back to Father Carter.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: What happened over there?!
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Yes! There were a few strange sounds at the start, like the moving of heavy objects, and then a loud bang and then silence.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: If you destroyed that sacred Chapel, we are all in trouble!
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Looks like my vision was true. Take a look at this.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: And the chapel is all good. You can go and check it out.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Father Carter was gone before you had finished the sentence. You heard him take the stairs two at a time, then a silence just long enough for a short prayer, then the stairs again, much faster.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: There’s water everywhere! Quick, get some towels and let's clean it up before the wood furniture gets affected!
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: We can even use this!
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: He snatched the pink cloth out of your hand to mop with. He did not get as far as the floor.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: What… is… this?!
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: I apologize, but it was necessary, and we shouldn’t use this cloth for cleaning. I will help with the cleaning!
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Yes. Yes, you will. Ayumi!
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Here, I already got some towels.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: So the three of you spent the next hour on your knees in the old chapel, mopping holy water out of the floorboards in the same sunbeam that had brought an angel down not long before.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: So, what’s that pink cloth? You seemed shocked after grabbing it, Father.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: I don’t know, yet, but it is imbued with divine energy, of that I’m certain. It’s the same as our sacred relics of the past, except this one is not a weapon. MC-NAME, what is this?
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: I do not know. Like I said, I had a vision that required Holy Water, a Holy Song, and the Sun, and that would get me some ‘proof’. Well, this is what I got.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: I see. Judging by the amount of water and your dry clothes, I'd guess you performed this ritual with a bit of improvisation, perhaps even... sans attire?
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: I plead the fifth!
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: Looks like I initially misjudged you, son. While you might not be the best person around, you are good-natured and might have some connection to the divine.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Father Carter handed you a card: Black Knights – Church Investigator ID.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: This is your access card. With this, you will be allowed to enter the ‘demonic zone’. You can even present this card at the Military HQ, and they will allow you to access their Black Knights Department.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: When you talk to me in the future, I can allow you access to certain zones, and the military can allow you access to other zones. We also have missions regarding what artifacts we are looking for.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Access to the ‘demonic zone’ is only available on weekends and Fridays. Please be prepared if you want to enter one. But for now, you should rest. It will take a few days to get the ID approved by the higher-ups and synced with the military.
nodes.speaker: Father Carter

nodes.text: Feel free to visit me downtown. I have a shop that specializes in matters of the heart, and perhaps it would be good to get to know each other better.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: I can also grant you access to some areas in the ‘demonic zone’ that only scouts can reach, should you need to venture there.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: May destiny guide our paths.
nodes.speaker: Ayumi

nodes.text: Welcome back, MC-NAME. You look like you've had quite the day.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: You could say that. It's been... enlightening.
nodes.speaker: You

nodes.text: I bet you have many questions still. Why don't you get some rest? We can talk more tomorrow.
nodes.speaker: Viviane

nodes.text: Thank you, MC-NAME. I’ll be here, guiding you.
nodes.speaker: Arielle

nodes.text: The prologue is complete.
nodes.title: The Casanova Killer
